text:
anna: quick thread to collect postmortem follow-ups for last night's node OOMs (kv slab-3). we saw repeated micro-alloc storms and poor free coalescing. listing owners and next steps.

mike: i pulled perf logs. timeline shows repeated allocation spikes at 01:52, 02:07, 02:23 UTC across 3 hosts. slab3 internal fragmentation jumped from 24% -> 82% in ~45m.

sophie: reproduced locally with a small-key churn harness (created TKT-1245). pattern: many tiny short-lived keys that prevent contiguous free runs.

kevin: proposed split of work:
- reproduce & perf harness improvements -> @sophie (TKT-1245)
- heap diff & allocation map -> @mike (GH#4602)
- runtime guardrails (soft limits + eviction pressure) -> @kevin (PR by 48h)
- alerting for fragmentation slope -> @anna (monitoring)

ops-bot: incident-bot: created INC-4931 for escalation and tracking.

anna: runbook fragments to try before rolling changes cluster-wide:
1) enable slab_coalesce_hint=true on canary
2) reduce KV_PREFIX_CACHE_MAX=8000 per shard for 12h
3) apply incremental_gc_rate=0.25 on canary

mike: uploaded two heap diffs: s3://redwood-debug/heapdiffs/1765454321.before and 1765454321.after. key observations: many 16B allocations pinned in slab3; we saw low free-block-merges in the allocator trace.

sophie: note: the local harness can reproduce the frag in <5m with default alloc patterns. i'll add it as a perf-check in CI (small smoke).

kevin: telemetry + alerting plan: add a synthetic rule that watches "slab3_frag_slope > 10%/15m" AND "eviction_rate > 50/s" -> page ops on-call and create auto-ticket INC-4931.

anna: timeline & owners recap:
- TKT-1245 (harness + repro) -> @sophie (24h)
- GH#4602 (heap diff analysis + allocation map) -> @mike (24h)
- PR for runtime guardrails (soft limits + incremental GC) -> @kevin (48h canary, 72h rollout)
- monitoring rule + dashboard -> @anna (48h)

mike: quick canary results after enabling coalesce_hint + reduced cache: peak resident mem down ~20% on canaries, fragmentation slope flattened. tail RPC latency unchanged.

sophie: adding a follow-up retro item: consider allocator improvement (better free-block merging heuristics) and documenting common allocation anti-patterns for SDKs.

kevin: i'll open GH#4610 for the guardrail PR and link tests. will ping when canary is live.

anna: thanks all. please update your tickets with links to logs & heap diffs. we'll do a short recap in next week's ops sync. ping here for blockers.
